participants: 10–15 ECS staff or students aged 18 or over
sequence: Round 1 A, about three minutes: textile-based arrangement, prepared examples, chosen postcard and optional caption
Round 1 B, about three minutes: full message/reply history and a related postcard made from a selected message
Optional printed copies of own cards without others’ replies
ai: Prepared and checked before sessions. Researcher manually switches examples and assembles cards.
data: A optional one-sentence caption and selected source/prepared-image references
B original messages, replies, clarifications, reply relationships and links between messages, sources, images and derived postcards
questions: Which prototype should we develop further for a museum experience? Tick one.
A: How did working from the textile object and comparing AI examples shape or change your understanding of authenticity? Why?
B: How did earlier messages, replies and the AI image affect what you expressed or understood across cultural perspectives?
Why your choice in Q1, and what would you improve in the activities, wall or take-away cards?
storage: Local wall restricted to study participants. Locked paper forms and University-approved secure UK digital storage.
retention: At least 10 years after collection or publication, whichever is later, then review disposal.
withdrawal: Skip or discard drafts before submission. Submitted anonymous cards and forms cannot be located for removal.
museum_stage: Later museum fieldwork requires a separate detailed plan.
relation: The first prototype round explores the two working concepts. Its limited implementation and data plan apply to this round.

research_questions.A: How do people maintain or revise their understandings of authenticity through interaction with AI and cultural heritage?
research_questions.B: How do people express and negotiate their understanding of a shared heritage object through AI-mediated cross-cultural exchange?
